title: float32/float64 arithmetic, conversion to int, float32 rounding and the float library
derivation: A float converts to int by truncation toward zero (-2.7 -> -2). 7 / 2.0 is float (3.5), *10 = 35. sqrt(2)*1000 = 1414.2 -> 1414; pow(2,10) = 1024; round(-2.5) rounds half away from zero, -3 (C round). half(9.0) = 4.5, *10 = 45. 0.1 as float64 times 1e9 is 100000000.00000001 -> 100000000; 0.1 rounded to float32 is 0.100000001490116..., times 1e9 -> 100000001, so the float32 is greater than the float64 (lt=1).
